items.s: At the market we bought apples___ pears and grapes.
items.tip: Use commas between things in a list. Before the last one, and is enough.

A full stop would end the sentence after apples, but the list goes on.
no.!: ! ends a sentence with a big feeling, but the list isn't finished yet.

items.say: At the market we bought apples, pears and grapes.
items.ask: At the market we bought apples pears and grapes.

items.s: Do you want rice___ noodles or soup?
items.tip: A list of choices has commas too: rice, noodles or soup.

A full stop would end the question too early. The choices go on.
no.?: The question mark goes at the very end, after soup.
no.': An apostrophe is for short forms (don't) or owning (Sam's), not for a list.

items.say: Do you want rice, noodles or soup?
items.ask: Do you want rice noodles or soup?

items.tip: Put a comma after Yes or No when you answer: Yes, please!

Yes. Please! makes two tiny sentences. We write Yes, please! with a little pause.
no.?: Yes isn't a question here. It's an answer.
no.': An apostrophe isn't a pause mark. After Yes we need a comma.

items.say: Yes, please!
items.ask: Yes please!

items.s: We saw red___ yellow and green peppers.
items.tip: Colours in a list are split by commas: red, yellow and green.

A full stop would end the sentence after red.
no.?: This sentence tells us something. It doesn't ask.
no.!: ! ends a sentence, but the list of colours goes on.

items.say: We saw red, yellow and green peppers.
items.ask: We saw red yellow and green peppers.

items.s: Can I have two bananas___ please?
items.tip: Put a comma before please at the end of a question: …, please?

A full stop would end the question before please.
no.?: The question mark comes at the very end, after please.
no.': An apostrophe isn't a pause mark. Before please we need a comma.

items.say: Can I have two bananas, please?
items.ask: Can I have two bananas please?

items.tip: Put a comma after No when you answer: No, thank you.

No. Thank you. is two short sentences. We write No, thank you. with a little pause.
no.?: No isn't asking anything here. It's an answer.
no.!: No! would sound very cross. A polite No, thank you. has a comma.

items.say: No, thank you.
items.ask: No thank you.

items.tip: Do you…? is a question, so it ends with a question mark.

Do you sell…? asks something, so it needs a question mark.
no.,: A comma can't end a sentence.
no.!: ! is for a big feeling. This sentence asks a question.

items.say: Do you sell watermelons?
items.ask: Do you sell watermelons

items.s: The stall sells cups, plates and bowls___
items.tip: The list is finished and the sentence tells us something, so end with a full stop.

no.,: bowls is the last thing in the list, so the sentence ends here with a full stop.
no.?: The sentence tells us what the stall sells. It doesn't ask.
no.': An apostrophe goes inside words like don't. It can't end a sentence.

items.say: The stall sells cups, plates and bowls.
items.ask: The stall sells cups, plates and bowls

items.tip: don't = do not. The apostrophe goes where the o is missing.

no.dont: don't is short for do not. It needs an apostrophe where the o is missing.
no.do'nt: The apostrophe goes where the letter is missing: do not → don't.
no.dont': The apostrophe goes in place of the missing o, between n and t.

items.say: I don't like spiders.
items.ask: I don't like spiders.

items.tip: It's = it is. The apostrophe takes the place of the i.

no.Its: Its (no apostrophe) means 'belonging to it'. For it is, write It's.
no.Its': There's no word Its'. It is → It's.
no.It'is: The apostrophe replaces the missing letter i: it is → it's.

items.say: It's my brother's birthday today.
items.ask: It's my brother's birthday today.

items.tip: I'm = I am. The apostrophe takes the place of the a.

no.Im: Im needs an apostrophe where the a is missing: I'm.
no.I'am: The apostrophe replaces the a, so it's I'm, not I'am.
no.im: This is the first word, and I is always a capital: I'm.

items.say: I'm ten years old.
items.ask: I'm ten years old.

items.tip: can't = cannot. The apostrophe goes where the letters are missing.

no.cant: can't needs an apostrophe: cannot → can't.
no.can'ot: We leave out n and o and write can't.
no.ca'nt: The apostrophe goes between n and t: can't.

items.say: We can't find the kitten anywhere!
items.ask: We can't find the kitten anywhere!

items.s: ___ going to the beach on Saturday.
items.tip: We're = we are. The apostrophe takes the place of the a.

no.Were: Were (no apostrophe) is the past of are: we were. For we are, write We're.
no.Wer'e: The apostrophe goes where the a is missing: We're.
no.We'are: The apostrophe replaces the a, so it's We're.

items.say: We're going to the beach on Saturday.
items.ask: We're going to the beach on Saturday.

items.tip: doesn't = does not. The apostrophe goes where the o is missing.

no.doesnt: doesn't needs an apostrophe where the o is missing.
no.does'nt: The apostrophe goes in place of the o in not: doesn't.
no.doe'snt: The apostrophe goes between n and t: doesn't.

items.say: My sister doesn't like broccoli.
items.ask: My sister doesn't like broccoli.

items.tip: There's = there is. The apostrophe takes the place of the i.

no.Theres: There's needs an apostrophe where the i is missing.
no.There'is: The apostrophe replaces the i, so it's There's.
no.Ther'es: The apostrophe goes after There: There's.

items.say: Look! There's a rainbow!
items.ask: Look! There's a rainbow!

items.tip: I'll = I will. The apostrophe takes the place of wi.

no.Ill: Ill means sick! For I will, write I'll.
no.I'l: I will keeps both l's: I'll.
no.il'l: I is always a capital, and the apostrophe goes after it: I'll.

items.say: Don't worry, I'll help you.
items.ask: Don't worry, I'll help you.

items.tip: Names of places start with a capital letter: Penang.

no.penang: Names of places always start with a capital letter: Penang.
no.Penang's: Penang's means 'of Penang'. Here we just need the place.
no.Penangs: There is only one Penang, so no -s.

items.say: We went to Penang in June.
items.ask: We went to Penang in June.

items.tip: Months start with a capital letter: December.

no.december: Months always start with a capital letter: December.
no.Decembers: It was one December, so no -s.
no.December's: December's means 'of December'. Here we just need the month.

items.say: Our holiday was in December.
items.ask: Our holiday was in December.

items.tip: What did you…? asks a question, so it ends with a question mark.

What did you eat? asks something, so it needs a question mark.
no.,: A comma can't end a sentence.
no.!: ! is for a big feeling. This sentence asks a question.

items.say: What did you eat there?
items.ask: What did you eat there

items.s: We ate noodles and ice kacang___
items.tip: A telling sentence ends with a full stop (or ! if you're very excited).

no.?: This sentence tells us what they ate. It doesn't ask.
no.,: The sentence is finished, so a comma can't end it.
no.': An apostrophe goes inside short words. It can't end a sentence.

items.say: We ate noodles and ice kacang.
items.ask: We ate noodles and ice kacang

items.s: What a hot day it was___
items.tip: What a…! shows a strong feeling, so it ends with an exclamation mark.

no.?: It starts with What, but it isn't a question. What a hot day! is a strong feeling.
no.,: A comma can't end a sentence.
no.': An apostrophe can't end a sentence. What a…! needs !.

items.say: What a hot day it was!
items.ask: What a hot day it was

items.s: My aunt ___ lives near the sea.
items.tip: People's names start with a capital letter: Rosa.

no.rosa: People's names always start with a capital letter: Rosa.
no.Rosas: Your aunt is one person called Rosa, so no -s.
no.ROSA: Only the first letter of a name is a capital: Rosa.

items.say: My aunt Rosa lives near the sea.
items.ask: My aunt Rosa lives near the sea.

items.tip: Languages start with a capital letter: English, Malay.

no.malay: Languages always start with a capital letter, like English and Malay.
no.Malays: Malays means Malay people. Here we need the language: Malay.
no.Malay's: Malay's means 'of Malay'. Here we just need the language.

items.say: She speaks English and Malay.
items.ask: She speaks English and Malay.

items.s: Will you come with us next time___
items.tip: Will you…? is a question, so it ends with a question mark.

Will you come…? asks something, so it needs a question mark.
no.,: A comma can't end a sentence.
no.!: ! is for a big feeling. This is a friendly question.

items.say: Will you come with us next time?
items.ask: Will you come with us next time
